title: Wave Equation and Wave Types
welcome_lead: Travel along a wave with v = f lambda and distinguish transverse from longitudinal motion.
meta_desc: A-Level Waves adventure on wave equation and classification of wave types.
final_note: Every wave obeys v = f lambda — from radio to gamma to sound.

concepts.def: Distance between two adjacent identical points.
Number of cycles per second, measured in Hz.
v = f lambda; how fast the wave moves.
Restricting transverse oscillations to one plane.

walkthroughs.body_html: v = f lambda relates speed (m/s), frequency (Hz) and wavelength (m). If frequency doubles at fixed speed, wavelength halves.
Oscillation is at right angles to direction of travel. These can be polarised. Examples: all electromagnetic waves and waves on strings.
Particles vibrate along the propagation direction creating compressions and rarefactions. They cannot be polarised. Example: sound in air.
